record.context_brief: Extremal interlacing counts for subgraph centrality
record.original_question: For a graph G with adjacency matrix A, define the subgraph centrality of a vertex i by SC(i, β) = [e^{βA}]_{ii}. Two non-cospectral vertices i and j interlace at β when SC(i, β) = SC(j, β); such a β is called an interlacing value. Given k ∈ N, characterize the smallest graph or graphs that contain a pair of vertices with at least k interlacing values for subgraph centrality. Conversely, for a graph on n vertices, determine the largest possible number of subgraph-centrality interlacing values that one pair of vertices can have, and in particular decide whether there are graph classes for which the general upper bound d − 1, where d is the number of distinct eigenvalues of A, is attained.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G be a finite simple graph with vertex set V(G) and adjacency matrix A. For a real parameter β, the subgraph centrality of a vertex i ∈ V(G) is defined by

  SC(i, β) = [e^{βA}]_{ii} = Σ_{k≥0} β^k [A^k]_{ii} / k!.

Two vertices i, j ∈ V(G) are called cospectral if [A^k]_{ii} = [A^k]_{jj} for every nonnegative integer k (equivalently, SC(i, β) = SC(j, β) for all β). Two non-cospectral vertices i and j are said to interlace at β if SC(i, β) = SC(j, β); such a value β is called an interlacing value of the pair (i, j). Let d denote the number of distinct eigenvalues of A; it is known that the number of interlacing values of any non-cospectral pair is at most d − 1.

Address the following:

(a) For each k ∈ ℕ, characterize the graph(s) of smallest order containing a pair of non-cospectral vertices with at least k interlacing values of the subgraph centrality.

(b) For each n ∈ ℕ, determine the maximum, over all graphs G on n vertices and all non-cospectral pairs (i, j) of vertices of G, of the number of interlacing values of (i, j).

(c) Decide whether there exist classes of graphs for which the upper bound d − 1 on the number of interlacing values of a non-cospectral pair is attained, and if so describe such classes.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem in the literature on subgraph centrality. Search results indicate that only partial examples are known (e.g., minimal graphs with up to two interlacing values, and a 60-vertex example with three interlacing values), and obtaining sharper bounds for specific graph classes and characterizing extremal graphs remain open.
